extracted.intended_audience: State air agencies/state plan developers, affected electric generating unit (EGU) operators, and EPA reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and documenting state plans under CAA section 111(d) that incorporate compliance flexibilities (emission trading, averaging, unit-specific mass-based compliance) for affected EGUs while demonstrating equivalent stringency to EPA presumptive standards of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: GHGRP reporting when CCS captures qualifying CO2
rubrics_metrics.description: Any affected unit that employs CCS technology that captures enough CO2 to meet the standard and injects the captured CO2 underground must report under GHGRP subpart RR or GHGRP subpart VV; if the emitting EGU sends captured CO2 offsite, it must transfer the CO2 to a facility subject to the GHGRP requirements, and the facility injecting the CO2 underground must report under GHGRP subpart RR or GHGRP subpart VV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with the standard is determined exclusively by the tons of CO2 captured by the emitting EGU (not the tons sequestered by the geologic site). The requirement to transfer captured CO2 to an entity subject to GHGRP is an enforcement element to avoid duplicative monitoring, reporting, and verification and does not change UIC permitting requirements or regulate downstream recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissibility of compliance flexibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is allowing the use of compliance flexibilities — emission trading, averaging, and unit-specific mass-based compliance — for affected EGUs in certain subcategories and circumstances under these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The allowance is tailored to ensure consistency with CAA section 111 and to maintain the stringency of the EPA's BSER determination; states are not required to include these flexibilities but may do so at their discretion. Flexibilities are used to demonstrate compliance with an already-established standard of performance, not to set the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to demonstrate equivalent stringency
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans that incorporate compliance flexibilities must demonstrate that use of such flexibilities will achieve a level of emission reduction that is in the aggregate as environmentally protective as each affected EGU individually achieving its rate-based standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This demonstration must show the plan overall achieves the same or better environmental outcome as application of the EPA's presumptive standards (after accounting for any application of RULOF). The EPA will review submissions to ensure consistency with CAA section 111's purpose of requiring sources to operate more cleanly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and documentation requirements for equivalence demonstrations
rubrics_metrics.description: In their plans, states must clearly demonstrate how they calculated the aggregate rate-based emission limitation, mass limit, or mass budget from unit-specific, rate-based presumptive standards of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must identify the specific affected EGUs participating, which flexibility each unit will use, the unit-specific rate-based presumptive standard, and the standard established in the plan for each unit or set of units. States must document and justify assumptions used in calculations (e.g., weighting, utilization levels) and explain how the flexibility will maintain the requisite stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rate-based averaging and trading assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate-based averaging and trading are easier to demonstrate as equivalent because the aggregate rate-based emission limitation or adjusted rate used for trading is calculated based on both emission output and gross generation output (utilization) of participating EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rate-based program inherently adjusts for changes in utilization and preserves the imperative to 'operate more cleanly,' providing relatively stronger assurance of equivalence compared to mass-based approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backstop emission rate requirement for mass-based mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For unit-specific mass-based compliance and mass-based trading, the EPA is requiring the use of a backstop emission limitation (backstop rate) in conjunction with the mass-based approach for both the long-term and medium-term coal-fired subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The backstop rate is required because a mass limit or budget alone may not guarantee emission reductions commensurate with cleaner performance; states must also show utilization assumptions are appropriately conservative. The backstop helps prevent units from complying merely by shifting generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptively approvable mass-based approach limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA is finalizing a presumptively approvable unit-specific mass-based compliance approach only for affected EGUs in the long-term coal-fired subcategory, and is not providing a presumptively approvable approach for medium-term coal-fired subcategory or for emission trading/averaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may attempt to design mass-based approaches for medium-term coal-fired EGUs, but EPA was unable to devise an implementable presumptively approvable approach and will review such proposals case-by-case against foundational principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of RULOF sources from trading/averaging and mass-based compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission trading or averaging programs must not include affected EGUs for which states have invoked RULOF to apply less stringent standards of performance; affected EGUs with a RULOF-based standard are also prohibited from using unit-specific mass-based compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RULOF sources have bespoke, individualized obligations and are unlikely to overperform; their participation could undermine equivalence by allowing other sources to obtain compliance instruments from less stringent RULOF sources. The heterogeneity and uncertainty from RULOF make mass-based designs unreliable for maintaining stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories from trading/averaging and mass-based compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission trading or averaging programs may not include affected EGUs in the natural gas- and oil-fired steam subcategories; these EGUs are also prohibited from using unit-specific mass-based compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Their BSER and degree of emission limitation do not require improvement and already account for varying efficiency at different operating levels; including them would be unlikely to add overperformance value and could undermine equivalence by enabling other units to underperform against more stringent standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope tailoring and limits to protect environmental outcomes and EJ concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of allowable flexibilities is tailored to ensure state plans maintain the stringency of the EPA's BSER determinations and corresponding degree of emission limitation; limitations (e.g., prohibiting certain subcategories, requiring backstop rates) are included to address environmental justice concerns and maintain intended environmental outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trading programs can be designed with features (like unit-specific emission rates) to help ensure reductions and benefits accrue proportionally to EJ communities. States must conduct meaningful engagement with stakeholders on plan elements including flexibilities, and may add further features or forgo flexibilities entirely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful engagement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to subpart Ba, states are required to conduct meaningful engagement on all aspects of their state plans with pertinent stakeholders, including any potential use of flexibilities like emission trading or averaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaningful engagement provides an opportunity for communities most affected and vulnerable to provide input on impacts from use of compliance flexibilities, and is part of the EPA's consideration when reviewing state plan satisfactoriness.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA case-by-case review of trading/averaging programs
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not providing a presumptively approvable approach to emission trading or averaging; instead, it will review emission trading or averaging programs in state plans on a case-by-case basis against foundational principles for consistency with CAA section 111.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must demonstrate how programs ensure at least equivalent stringency; EPA will evaluate the program design, assumptions, and whether aggregate emissions are at least as protective as unit-specific compliance with presumptive standards (after accounting for RULOF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibilities do not alter underlying standard of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any flexibilities involving aggregate compliance are used to demonstrate compliance with an already-established standard of performance and do not alter the benchmark of emission performance against which compliance is evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compliance flexibility may change how an affected EGU demonstrates compliance (e.g., surrender allowances from another unit) but does not change the presumptive standard; RULOF remains the mechanism to apply a different, individualized standard of performance where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan must address every affected EGU and preserve EPA's level of emission reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: To be found 'satisfactory' by the EPA, a state plan that includes compliance flexibilities must address each affected EGU within the state and demonstrate that the plan overall achieves at least the level of emission reduction that would result if each affected EGU was achieving its presumptive standard of performance (after accounting for any application of RULOF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes providing unit-level allocations/limits or showing how aggregate limits translate to unit-level outcomes, documenting assumptions, and ensuring mechanisms (e.g., backstop rates) are in place to prevent erosion of emission reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for coal subcategories and cross-subcategory trading decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA allows both medium- and long-term coal-fired subcategories to participate in all types of compliance flexibilities (within EPA parameters) and is not finalizing a restriction on trading or averaging across those two coal subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA believes incentivizing overperformance in these coal subcategories is appropriate (including for units receiving IRC section 45Q credits) and that trading across the medium- and long-term coal subcategories may be allowed provided state plans still demonstrate equivalent stringency.
